newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
SONIA JOINS CONGRESS PARTY

The Congress party announced that Sonia Gandhi had become a primary member of the party since March 21. Her close associates believe she will eventually take over the party leadership. Since Sonia Gandhi had become only a primary member and not an active member (who only could hold a party post or be elected on any of the party committees), she evidently would not contest the forthcoming party elections. As per the party constitution, one can become an active member by enrolling 25 primary members.
The Pioneer
ELECTION COMMISSION GIVES CONGRESS MORE TIME

The Election Commission granted 15 days time beyond May 31 for the Congress party to complete its organisational elections. The commission asked some clarifications from the Janata Dal after which it may also get time to complete its organisational polls. The rescheduled organisational election of the Congress would culminate with the simultaneous election of All India Congress Committee (AICC) members and the party president on June 9. Alongwith AICC members, state Congress Committee presidents, office bearers and executives would also be elected.
The Hindustan Times
BOFORS REPORT TO BE SUBMITTED SHORTLY

The chief of the Central Bureau of Investigations (CBI) said the agency was expecting a set of documents related to bank accounts in the Bofors gun deal to he handed over to it by Swiss authorities by June end. He said this set of documents was not given to the CBI as some cases related to them were in progress in Swiss courts. Final touches were being given to the CBI report on its probe into the 640 million rupee Bofors case, which would be submitted to the government within a few days, CBI sources said. On receipt of the report, the government would decide whether it could grant sanction to the CBI to prosecute the accused.
The Economic Times
NEGATIVE CAPITAL GOODS GROWTH BLURS INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT

Growth in the domestic capital goods sector, one of the key reflectors of industrial production trends, has suddenly slumped and turned negative since November last. This was in sharp contrast with the 16.6 percent growth in capital goods production during the first seven months of 1996/97 (April-March). The Economic Survey for 1996/97 had noted the trend of healthy growth in the capital goods production. It appeared to have reversed its course since November and in January 1997 witnessed a negative growth of 3.2 percent against a growth of 19.5 percent in January 1996.
DTH BEAM LIKELY TO SPAN COUNTRYWIDE

The draft Broadcast Bill takes a liberal view on direct to home (DTH) services by removing restrictions on territory. It, however, proposes limiting the number of local delivery services cable networks to have strict regulation and better control over the networks. According to the proposed law, DTH licensees would be permitted to cover the entire country and would not be restricted to one or two regions, as proposed earlier. The draft law had also recommended that both cable operators and DTH broadcasters would be allowed to introduce their own programmes into the packages they would offer to subscribers.
BANK SHARES HIT THE ROOF IN HECTIC TRADING

Shares of government and private banks shot up in the National bourse (NSE) but trading in pivotals and other frontline stocks remained at a low ebb. While bank shares were in the limelight following the announcement of the credit policy, the spurt took marketmen by surprise since no major policy announcement benefiting the sector was made.
KUMARMANGALAM BIRLA PONDERS BOLD RECAST

The 150 billion rupee Aditya Birla Group might undertake its first steps towards a sweeping restructuring of its operations in the near future. Such an exercise, on a scale unprecedented in the history of corporate India, would take at least a year to complete. It would also mark the coming of age of Aditya Birla's son and successor Kumarmangalam. The idea would be to club together similar businesses and ultimately bring greater focus to the group, which at the moment looked as if it could do with some sharp shooting.
Financial Express
CORPORATES TO TAP OVER $1 BLN VIA ECB ROUTE

Corporates are vying with each other to tap the international debt market following the recent relaxation in external commercial borrowings (ECB) norm. Around 20 corporates have mandated their investment bankers to help garner funds through ECB route. These companies will mop up around one billion dollars in the next few months. The trend followed a notification issued by the Finance Ministry on April 2. The new policy removed end-use restrictions. Well known bankers like ING Barings, Natwest Markets, United Bank of Switzerland, HSBC, ANZ Grindlays, Citibank and others are pitching for these accounts.
INDUSTRY APEX BODY FORECASTS EIGHT PERCENT GDP GROWTH

The new president of the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII) expressed confidence in the industry's ability to overcome the economic slump witnessed last year. The CII forecast eight percent gross domestic product growth in 1997/98 (April-March) along with a 12 percent industrial growth. It was very confident that the economy would revive as its fundamentals were very good. The CII was sure that investments would go up and there would be growth in industry. Commenting on the low four percent growth in exports last year against Cll's prediction of 20 percent, the new president said it was a year plagued by problems.
POWERGRID TO ENTER INFORMATION SUPERHIGHWAY

PowerGrid Corporation plans to offer long distance telecom carrier service by leasing its vast transmission infrastructure and capability to install optical fibre cables. It was expecting a return of its entire investment over a period of four to five years. PowerGrid proposed leasing its facilities to the Department of Telecommunication and other government telecom companies, private operators in basic and cellular telephony and cable TV.
Business Standard
$1 BILLION ECBS CLEARED IN APRIL

The Finance Ministry approved over $1 billion in external commercial borrowings (ECBs) in the first few weeks of the current fiscal year beginning April. The rush to raise ECBs came at a time when the domestic markets were flush with liquidity and domestic interest rates were on a downward trend. Government officials saw this as a pointer towards fresh investments in infrastructure. Cellular telecom companies AT&T Birla and Sterling Cellular received ECB clearances worth $250 million and $80 million respectively. AT&T Birla had mandated Bank of America and Toronto Dominion Bank to raise $250 million.
STANDARD & POORS BUYS ADB STAKE IN CRISIL

Standard and Poors (S&P), the world's largest rating service, bought out Asian Development Bank's 9.6 percent stake in Credit Rating Information Services of India (Crisil). S&P signed an agreement acquiring the entire ADB stake in Crisil. Since the acquisition was a negotiated deal, the price was kept a secret. The transfer of shares was subject to approval by the Reserve Bank of India.
Business Line
ADB TO INVEST $ 500 MLN IN INDIA

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) planned to fund core projects in India to the tune of about $800 million in 1997. The thrust areas of ADB funding would be power, ports and housing. The bank may also participate in the newly created Infrastructure Finance Development Corporation through equity and loans. The quantum of equity and loan would be finalised soon.
The Observer
TELEVISION MAKERS MIGHT FACE PROBE

Television manufacturing companies might face a probe by the revenue department for buying colour picture tubes (CTPs) from the grey market causing loss to the exchequer. The Department of Electronics (DoE) said the number of colour picture tubes sold in the domestic market and the number of televisions manufactured in the country for 1996/97 (April-March) did not match. As per the figures available with the DoE, two million CPTs were sold in the domestic market, including the total number of imported CPTs. But the total number of televisions manufactured during this period was 2.6 million.
RAILWAY BUDGET APPROVED

Parliament approved the Railway Budget for 1997/98 (April-March) with the upper house returning relevant appropriation bills by a voice vote. The railway minister said the government was working on modalities to make the build-operate-lease-transfer more attractive to bring in larger private sector investment. Encouraged by the success of he own-your-wagon scheme, the railways was considering taking a lenient view of the demand of private investors to enhance project cost by eliminating the cost over run and other factors incurred by railways in their earlier projects.
BOMBAY AIRPORT FEASIBILITY ACCORD SIGNED

A memorandum of understanding (MoU) to develop an international airport and infrastructure facilities in Bombay was signed between Indian and British firms. The companies would look into potential sites and infrastructure needs for the airport, carry out environmental and planning studies and study the scope for extending the existing airport's economic life. The airport's capacity might reach saturation point by the early 21st century.
